## Bearer

WatchRaceNavigator — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/race/WatchRaceNavigator.kt

## Trigger

checkInactivity, called with the current elapsed-realtime clock — observed
only from tests; no production call site was found (MainActivity and the
race screens never call it), but the fix is internal to the method's own
comparison and does not depend on that call site existing.

## Today

checkInactivity computes `elapsed = nowElapsedRealtime - lastInteractionAtElapsedRealtime`
and returns to MAIN when `elapsed >= INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS` (WatchRaceNavigator.kt,
line 152), so the instant exactly at the 8-second boundary already counts as
expired. Every sensor freshness window in the project follows the opposite
rule: SensorFreshnessWindow.evaluate (core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/sensor/Freshness.kt)
computes `age = now - lastReadingAt` and stays Fresh while `age <= WINDOW_MS`,
so the instant exactly at its window's boundary still counts as valid.

## Expected

checkInactivity treats the instant exactly at INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS as still
within the timeout, matching SensorFreshnessWindow.evaluate's boundary rule —
the comparison becomes `elapsed > INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS` rather than
`elapsed >= INACTIVITY_TIMEOUT_MS`.
